name: Vilnius University
description: One of the oldest universities in Central and Eastern Europe, founded in 1579, with linked courtyards and a Yiddish institute.

name: Monument to Romain Gary
description: A statue of a boy holding a shoe, honoring the French writer Romain Gary, who spent part of his childhood on this street.

name: Vilnius TV Tower
description: A 326-meter TV tower where Soviet troops killed unarmed civilians on January 13, 1991.

name: Vilna Gaon monument
description: A bust of the Vilna Gaon, an 18th-century rabbi and scholar, on a street of the old Jewish quarter.

name: Vilnius Cathedral
description: The city’s main Catholic cathedral, rebuilt in neoclassical style in the late 1700s, with a freestanding bell tower on its square.
